progress_reporting.when: After each implemented screen, before switching workspace or handoff. Propose only tested items; identify the build and limitations. Do not duplicate unchanged pending/accepted work. Human approval still required.

delivery_gate.rule:
A screen or workspace is unfinished until its working UI, F1 contextual help, English/Urdu screen handbook,
workspace guide and detailed FAQ for every supported role, bounded 100-250% keyboard zoom, frontend coverage checks,
and named human review of fresh, newly created data and supported CRUD operations are complete. Follow the workspace review
checklist (guide 17). Missing evidence stays pending; seeded-demo browsing, API tests or screenshots alone do not
establish completion. Agents propose evidence; only authenticated human review accepts progress.

compulsory.label: F1 contextual help
compulsory.what: F1 opens the correct permitted help, including from fields/dialogs, preserves unsaved work and restores focus. Visible Help also works; login/locked/kiosk help exposes only public/operator guidance.

compulsory.label: Complete role-specific FAQs
compulsory.what: Every supported role task in this workspace, including shared screens and handovers, has a detailed reviewed English/Urdu FAQ. Follow get_handbook_outline; a generic FAQ or an unreviewed role journey is unfinished.

compulsory.label: Keyboard zoom: 100-250% only
compulsory.what: Ctrl++/Ctrl+=, Ctrl+- and Ctrl+0 (Command on macOS), Settings and all enabled zoom routes share one state clamped to 100-250%. Test both bounds, reset, persistence and usable English/Urdu layouts at 250%.

compulsory.label: Human review with newly created data
compulsory.what: A named human follows guide 17 on this build: creates new synthetic records through the UI and verifies read, update/correction and permitted delete/cancel/deactivate paths, refusal paths and handovers. Read-only screens use fresh upstream records. Record IDs and evidence; pre-existing demo data alone is insufficient.

zoom.one_state: The keys, the Settings slider and any menu, wheel or pinch zoom move ONE zoom state, clamped to 100.0-250.0 %, saved as ui_scale_pct (PUT /settings/me) and restored at login (/auth/me preferences). Electron: webContents.setZoomFactor(pct / 100).

delivery_gate.workspace_done_when: Every screen of the workspace has every compulsory item above, in addition to its endpoints, events and rules: F1 contextual Help, a detailed FAQ for every role of the workspace (English and Urdu), the bounded keyboard zoom and a named human's review with newly created data (get_guide('workspace-review-checklist')), signed on the portal. Missing any one, the workspace is NOT done: report it as pending, never as complete.

requirements.title: Establish the purpose and staff context
requirements.instruction:
Before choosing a layout, state who is doing what, what starts the task, what success looks like and what could
confuse them. Use the screen's purpose, workspace, playbook and demo role. Distinguish a busy reception counter,
bedside nursing, a laboratory scanner and an office review. Record the relevant input devices, interruptions,
language and display conditions. Keep the patient, visit, money or stock context clear throughout the task.

Write down why the proposed interaction fits this work. Use actual staff-task evidence and references approved by
the frontend lead; do not substitute an attractive generic dashboard for the job. Do not invent software screens
for staff whose specified interaction is a physical badge tap.

requirements.title: Reuse intent through complete patterns
requirements.instruction:
Use the frontend team's approved design system and record its version and owner. Where no shared system has been
approved, use the team's established components within the backend constraints and record the outstanding decision.
Reuse complete patterns: patient selection and identity, search and selection, a validated write and its result,
pending approval and handover, printing and recovery, corrections to finalized records. Follow the relevant
playbook; a template must preserve the permissions and transitions of this particular task.

Document the reason for a variation. Explore alternatives where they make a task clearer or reduce effort, then
review them in the whole journey. Do not introduce arbitrary colours, motion, alerts or different meanings for the
same control. Read the relevant standards when building or reviewing the flow; do not rely on an old chat summary.

requirements.title: Complete the interaction and its recovery
requirements.instruction:
For every task show prerequisites, editable and read-only information, validation, the pending state, the confirmed
result and the next step. Distinguish loading, empty, unavailable, denied, stale and failed states. Explain disabled
actions when the user needs to know how to proceed. Include keyboard and scanner interactions, focus after actions,
confirmation, cancellation and navigation with unsaved work.

Use each endpoint's repeat rules, version checks and reconciliation instructions after an uncertain result. Never
show success merely because a button was pressed, queue clinical or money writes offline, or offer an unsupported
undo. Follow the existing guides for printing, reconnects, sessions, realtime refreshes and in-memory form recovery.
Never persist a co-signer's credentials. Distinguish server-owned rules from frontend presentation choices.

requirements.title: Make the details work in the actual environment
requirements.instruction:
Review both Light and DarkHighContrast, 100-250 percent zoom, English and Urdu, right-to-left layout, mixed-direction
identifiers, long names and dense tables. Bundle the required Urdu font. Keep meaning available through text and
icons, not colour alone. Verify labels, focus order, keyboard operation and readable status messages using the
frontend's accessibility tests and a person using the app.

Keyboard zoom shortcuts are compulsory: Ctrl++ (including Ctrl+=) increases, Ctrl+- decreases, and Ctrl+0 resets
to 100%; use Command on macOS. Clamp the application's zoom to **100% through 250%, inclusive**. Settings, keyboard,
menu and any enabled wheel/pinch zoom must share that bound and one zoom state. Persist `ui_scale_pct` through
`PUT /settings/me` and restore it on login; do not layer CSS scaling over an independent browser zoom. Touch clients
must expose equivalent visible controls and handle shortcuts when a hardware keyboard is attached. Test both bounds,
reset, intermediate values, reopened windows and dense forms/tables without clipped controls or lost data.

Use the actual terminal workflow and supported devices: a scanner must not type into the wrong field, a printer
problem must leave the task understandable, and a realtime update must not silently change the selected patient.
Review consistency across screens and helpful details such as an explicit selected date, shift or patient. Give
the product character through clarity, wording and care for staff, within the approved visual system. Any new
performance target or clinical presentation rule needs its designated owner's decision.

requirements.title: Teach the delivered UI as part of building it
requirements.instruction:
Create or revise the screen handbook and the workspace guide with its role-specific FAQ in the same change as
the UI. Follow `get_end_user_handbook_brief` and `get_handbook_outline(workspace)` and the
[end-user handbook contract](12-end-user-handbook.md). Explain every user-facing control and meaningful outcome,
including frontend-only filters, navigation and dialogs that have no API call. Use actual labels and demo-data
screenshots in English and Urdu; flag translations awaiting human review.

Cover every supported job task in the role's workspace FAQ, including shared screens and handovers. A help page's
existence does not establish completeness. Kiosks also need an operator job aid available through the authorized
staff help or training material; do not add a login to the kiosk to deliver it.

requirements.title: Require evidence before reporting completion
requirements.instruction:
A screen or workspace is unfinished until its working UI, F1 contextual help, English/Urdu screen handbook,
workspace guide and detailed FAQ for every supported role, bounded 100-250% keyboard zoom, frontend coverage checks,
and named human review of fresh, newly created data and supported CRUD operations are complete. Follow the workspace review
checklist (guide 17). Missing evidence stays pending; seeded-demo browsing, API tests or screenshots alone do not
establish completion. Agents propose evidence; only authenticated human review accepts progress.

The frontend repository must make these checks part of its build or CI:

- Maintain an inventory of implemented screens, workspaces, supported role tasks and interactive controls. Map each
  to handbook pages and sections in both languages. Include frontend-only behaviour; catalogue tasks are a minimum.
- Fail on missing or empty pages/sections, uncovered tasks or controls, broken help links or missing referenced
  screenshots. Test F1, screen Help, workspace Help, offline help, deep links, search and permission filtering; changing
  user or roles must not retain another user's navigation or search results.
- Run the relevant API scenario and frontend interaction tests, including repeat submissions, concurrent edits,
  uncertain outcomes and hardware failures. A non-applicable case needs a reason, not a silent omission.
- Apply every section of the [human workspace acceptance checklist](17-workspace-review-checklist.md) to each role
  and supported task. Create fresh synthetic records through the UI, then read, update and cancel/deactivate/delete
  only as the API permits. Test refusal where deletion or editing is forbidden. Read-only roles inspect new records
  created by an authorized upstream role. Record the actual new IDs and outcomes; never treat seeded records alone
  or an agent's API calls as a human journey pass.
- Record the standards revision, implemented scope, test results, guide paths, demo screenshots and outstanding
  decisions in the change's review evidence. A named human reviewer must walk through a complete role journey using
  only the handbook, check that it matches the UI and review translations. Revise misleading or incomplete details.

The frontend lead owns the component and flow patterns, the delivery checks and their maintenance. The designated
clinical/language owners approve their wording and decisions. The backend supplies the contract and examples.
MCP supplies requirements, not proof that a frontend file exists, that a build passed or that staff can use it.
An agent may critique the work and collect evidence; it cannot approve its own human review or award progress.

checklist.title: Identify the implementation and complete scope
checklist.instruction:
- [ ] Record implementation ID/name, repository, commit/build, backend/standards revision, workspace, roles,
  reviewer, date, device/OS, languages and peripherals tested (the review's *Start* step: the portal fills in what it
  knows).
- [ ] Inventory each role's screens, tasks, controls, permissions and required handovers. Every task needs a test
  result and matching FAQ answer. A read-only role or non-applicable operation needs a specific contract-based reason.

checklist.title: Create fresh data through the frontend
checklist.instruction:
- [ ] With the review code in your app's DEV settings, create new records through each applicable create form:
  patient/visit, request/order, master record, transaction or register entry. The review lists them with their IDs as
  the server sees them; where a free-text field permits it, you may type the code there too, to find them again.
- [ ] Try required fields missing, invalid values, duplicate identifiers and cancellation before saving. Verify
  the visible validation, server refusal and that no partial or duplicate business record is reported as saved.
- [ ] Complete the valid path and check the generated number, defaults, ownership, patient/visit context and next step.
  A seeded master may be a prerequisite; the transaction being accepted must be new. Do not create destructive test
  masters on a shared server without coordinating with its backend team.

checklist.title: Read and retrieve those new records
checklist.instruction:
- [ ] Find each new record by its actual ID/number and relevant search/filter/sort controls. Open list and detail
  views, refresh, navigate away/back and sign in again. Confirm persistence and exact values, units, dates and status.
- [ ] Check empty/no-match results and pagination where applicable. A read-only role must read a fresh record created
  by an authorized upstream role and demonstrate that write actions are unavailable/refused.

checklist.title: Update, correct and exercise permitted deletion
checklist.instruction:
- [ ] Edit each supported field on the new record, save and re-read it. Check cancellation, unsaved-work navigation,
  stale versions and simultaneous edits from a second session; one user's changes must not silently replace another's.
- [ ] Test the actual permitted lifecycle: delete a draft where supported, or cancel, deactivate, stop, reverse or
  append a correction with the required reason/approval. Verify list/detail/history and downstream effects afterwards.
- [ ] Where deletion or editing is forbidden (for example finalized clinical or financial records), verify the
  frontend offers the permitted correction and the server refuses the forbidden action. Never invent hard deletion
  to tick a CRUD box. Record an explicit not-applicable/refused result with the supporting contract.

checklist.title: Permissions, handovers and end-to-end outcomes
checklist.instruction:
- [ ] Test allowed and denied actions with the appropriate accounts, including separation of requester/approver,
  sign-off, counter-signature and multi-role switching. Check patient and workspace context after every switch.
- [ ] Follow the new record into the next role's queue and complete the supported journey. Verify live refresh,
  balances/stock/bed state where relevant, notifications and printable output against the new record's values.
- [ ] Shared task coverage belongs to every role that uses it; do not mark a workspace done with an unfinished handover.

checklist.title: F1 help and detailed role FAQs
checklist.instruction:
- [ ] Press **F1** on each screen and with a field/dialog focused. Correct contextual help must open without losing
  input; closing it restores focus. Test visible Help, workspace help, offline reading, search and deep links.
- [ ] Follow each role task's FAQ using only its instructions. Check prerequisites, actual labels, steps, outcomes,
  errors, recovery and handovers in English and Urdu. Missing/generic answers fail acceptance.
- [ ] Change user/permissions and verify restricted pages/search results disappear. Login/locked/kiosk help must
  reveal only permitted public/operator guidance. Hardware keyboard shortcuts and touch Help must both work where supported.

checklist.title: Zoom, language and usable layouts
checklist.instruction:
- [ ] Test Ctrl++/Ctrl+=, Ctrl+-, Ctrl+0 (Command equivalents on macOS), Settings and any enabled wheel/pinch/menu
  routes. Verify **100% minimum, 250% maximum**, reset to 100%, persistence and a single shared application zoom state.
- [ ] Repeatedly try beyond both bounds. Test at 100%, 150%, 200% and 250%, in both themes and languages, including
  Urdu reading direction, long labels, tables, dialogs, validation messages and Help. All actions remain reachable.
- [ ] Check tab order, focus, scanner input and visible controls on touch clients. Do not confuse OS magnification
  with the application's saved zoom preference.

checklist.title: Failures, retries and devices
checklist.instruction:
- [ ] Test double submit, lost reply, disconnect/reconnect, session expiry, stale data and refused operations on
  the new records. Confirm honest pending/error messages, correct reconciliation and no duplicate writes.
- [ ] Test required printers/scanners/cameras, denied device permission and unavailable hardware. Verify recovery
  preserves appropriate form context and does not display success before the server confirms it.
- [ ] Patient workflows: register and admit a new patient **without** a photo (the form must let you skip it with no
  reason), then take one and see it on the patient and the admission; a PDF as the photo must be refused. Upload a
  synthetic outside report with its facility and date, re-open it under the correct patient and check it is labelled
  as an outside report, never shown as this hospital's result.

checklist.title: Keep reproducible evidence
checklist.instruction:
- [ ] The review on the portal is the evidence, kept on the DEV server: what the server saw your app do (records new
  and existing, refusals, each operation by lifecycle step and screen), your answers and a note for every Fail and N/A
  (what failed and how to reproduce it, or why it does not apply). Keep screenshots and longer test output with your
  app; mention where in the note.
- [ ] *Test in the app* is a to-do list that ticks itself: an operation turns **Done on a new record** when the server
  sees your app do it with the code, **Done on existing records only** when it changed demo data alone (the inspectors
  see that), **Refused** when you tested a refusal. Mark only what is not seen: *Not applicable* or *Fail*, with the note.
- [ ] *Screens*: for each screen, F1 help, the role FAQs and zoom (one click passes a whole column; then mark the
  exceptions). The **fresh-data** column is the server's: it passes where your app made new records with that screen's
  own write operations (any new record, for a screen that only reads); you can only reject it.
- [ ] *Export* gives the review as one Markdown file for your repository or review system, whenever you want it.
- [ ] Accepting or reporting **F1 help, the role FAQs, zoom or the fresh-data review** (on a proposal, on *Save this
  screen* or in the transfer of legacy work) needs **your signed review** of that screen's workspace. The portal
  preselects the review that passes them and refuses, saying why (`details.field` = `review_id`), an item without a
  signed review, on a review that does not cover the screen or one that does not pass it there. The backend team's
  inspectors see the review beside your agent's proposals.
- [ ] **Approve all reported progress** is one human declaration for the displayed selection; untick any untested items
  first. Each proposal retains its build, the review it was accepted with and your decision.

checklist.title: Decide and report honestly
checklist.instruction:
- [ ] Every applicable task and mandatory quality check must pass. A blocker, missing FAQ, broken F1, out-of-bounds
  zoom or untested fresh-data lifecycle keeps the screen/workspace pending. Partial item acceptance remains possible.
- [ ] The named human signs the review for this build (its *Sign* step: every question answered or decided by the
  server, the declaration that the writes with the code are theirs, not their agent's), clears the code from the app,
  accepts only tested proposal items or reports them manually, and returns failures: the agent reads the signed
  review's failures and notes (`progress_proposals` → `human_reviews`). Agents cannot start, fill or sign a review, nor
  approve their own claims. Backend inspection can confirm or withdraw accepted claims; verified points are a subset of
  completion, never an additional award.
- [ ] Retest affected tasks after fixes or backend changes; stale evidence does not establish the new build's behavior.

human_review.workspace_checklist:
- [ ] **Create:** open your cash shift on My cash shift, on a PC mapped to the Pharmacy Counter; dispense a
  prescription the doctor wrote in this review (in part, then the rest), an OTC sale for cash and one by card, a
  charity override request, a query on an unclear order.
- [ ] **Read:** the queue, the dispensed batches (chosen by the server, never by you) and the receipt; your drawer's
  expected cash after the cash sale, and My cash shift's F1 help in Pharmacy Counter.
- [ ] **Update / correct:** identify a patient's own medicine; for an order that must change, query it and see the
  line come back stopped or changed by the doctor; close your cash shift with the counted cash.
- [ ] **Cancel / delete:** withdraw the query.
- [ ] **Refused:** an OTC sale of a Schedule-H or high-alert medicine; stopping a medication line yourself
  (`FORBIDDEN`: the doctor stops it); Cash with no drawer open at the Pharmacy Counter (Cash unavailable, or
  `SHIFT_NOT_OPEN` naming your drawer at another counter), while Card still works.
- [ ] **Hand over:** the override reaches the zakat officer; the pharmacy clearance stage reaches the discharge desk.
human_review.operations_rule: Exercise each operation on records you create new in this review, through the app: create, then read them back, update or correct them, and cancel, withdraw or delete them where the contract allows (and see the refusal where it does not). The other_actions are the steps of the record's life (sign, approve, dispense ...).
human_review.portal_review: The human tester records this review on the portal (My progress → the workspace → Start the review), with its code in the app's DEV settings: the server sees the operations the app did on new records, the tester answers the rest and signs. The four compulsory items need that signed review; fresh data needs the server's evidence. You build the Review code setting (dev_build_headers), never start, fill or sign a review; progress_proposals → human_reviews lists the failures to fix.

send: X-Haspataal-Review: <the DEV settings' Review code, while the tester has one set>
dev_build_headers.review_code_setting: One app-wide field, Review code, in Settings → This terminal (open before login too), empty by default; the shared API client adds the header. Not on any screen or the login form.
dev_build_headers.release_build: The field and all three headers behind the DEV build flag (compiled out, never a runtime switch): the hospital's release build has neither (guide 19, I6 and I9).
dev_build_headers.never: Never set a review code yourself, in tests or scripts: only the tester's writes with it count.

verification.rule: Requirements only. Frontend CI checks coverage; a named human reviews the working journey.

screen.title: Dispense
screen.purpose: Dispense Now (partial allowed); server picks batches FEFO; take payment.

rule_objects.text: Clear the PharmacyClearance discharge stage once the patient's unused medicines are returned.

Read discharge-status to confirm the patient identity and blocked_on PharmacyClearance before clearing. After a lost answer re-read the stage's status, cleared_by_name and cleared_at there; never retry automatically.

A high-alert line (high_alert_category): a second person (pharmacist, or the nurse or doctor collecting it) checks the order and the medicine and co-signs with checker_username/_password (HIGH_ALERT_CHECK_REQUIRED; DUAL_CONTROL_SAME_PERSON). Show lasa_with next to the medicine: 'looks like …'.
After dispensing print one label per medicine: GET /dispensations/{dispensation_id}/labels (label printer).
PRESCRIPTION_QUERY_OPEN: the line waits for the doctor's answer to a query (Order queries screen).
Never let the user pick a batch — FEFO is server-side.
OPD pharmacy is cash-and-carry; credit only via approved Zakat/charity (charity_approval_id).

Cash goes into the user's own open shift at the Pharmacy Counter only: before offering Cash, GET /finance/cash-shifts/mine?node=PharmacyCounter. Null: Cash unavailable until it is opened on My cash shift (Card still works). SHIFT_NOT_OPEN with details.open_shift: the user's drawer is open at another counter (details.open_shift.node), which pharmacy cash never goes into; say so, never borrow another person's shift.

Exists for the service dispensing (work): show it as GET /establishment views.screens says for screen_id dispense (full; open_work: without its new work, with the banner "No new ... from now on"; records: history and corrections only; setup: only from Facility settings; hidden: in no menu), after login and again on establishment.changed. Never decide it from the profile's category.
POST /prescriptions/{prescription_id}/dispense continues dispensing work started earlier: offer it while dispensing is Active or Retiring (GET /establishment).

views.full: Show it; every action the user's permissions allow.
views.open_work: The service is Retiring: show it with the banner 'No new <new_work> from now on' and its open work; hide the actions that start new work of it (x-capability-gates; continues_while_retiring ones stay); keep every other action (completing, transferring, settling, correcting).
views.records: The service is Retired (or Preparing after it ran): show it as records only, under a 'Records' marker: lists, details, prints and the corrections the server still accepts; no action that starts new work.
views.setup: Not in the daily menus: reach it from Facility settings (a preview's prerequisites link to it) to set the service up before switching it on.
views.hidden: Not in any menu: the service has never run here, so the screen has nothing to show.

service.how: GET /establishment after login and on establishment.changed: views.screens gives this screen's view (one frontend build for every profile; never decide it from the profile's category)

progress_reporting.when: After each implemented screen, before switching workspace or handoff. Propose only tested items; identify the build and limitations. Do not duplicate unchanged pending/accepted work. Human approval still required.

delivery_gate.rule:
A screen or workspace is unfinished until its working UI, F1 contextual help, English/Urdu screen handbook,
workspace guide and detailed FAQ for every supported role, bounded 100-250% keyboard zoom, frontend coverage checks,
and named human review of fresh, newly created data and supported CRUD operations are complete. Follow the workspace review
checklist (guide 17). Missing evidence stays pending; seeded-demo browsing, API tests or screenshots alone do not
establish completion. Agents propose evidence; only authenticated human review accepts progress.

compulsory.label: F1 contextual help
compulsory.what: F1 opens the correct permitted help, including from fields/dialogs, preserves unsaved work and restores focus. Visible Help also works; login/locked/kiosk help exposes only public/operator guidance.

compulsory.label: Complete role-specific FAQs
compulsory.what: Every supported role task in this workspace, including shared screens and handovers, has a detailed reviewed English/Urdu FAQ. Follow get_handbook_outline; a generic FAQ or an unreviewed role journey is unfinished.

compulsory.label: Keyboard zoom: 100-250% only
compulsory.what: Ctrl++/Ctrl+=, Ctrl+- and Ctrl+0 (Command on macOS), Settings and all enabled zoom routes share one state clamped to 100-250%. Test both bounds, reset, persistence and usable English/Urdu layouts at 250%.

compulsory.label: Human review with newly created data
compulsory.what: A named human follows guide 17 on this build: creates new synthetic records through the UI and verifies read, update/correction and permitted delete/cancel/deactivate paths, refusal paths and handovers. Read-only screens use fresh upstream records. Record IDs and evidence; pre-existing demo data alone is insufficient.

zoom.one_state: The keys, the Settings slider and any menu, wheel or pinch zoom move ONE zoom state, clamped to 100.0-250.0 %, saved as ui_scale_pct (PUT /settings/me) and restored at login (/auth/me preferences). Electron: webContents.setZoomFactor(pct / 100).

delivery_gate.workspace_done_when: Every screen of the workspace has every compulsory item above, in addition to its endpoints, events and rules: F1 contextual Help, a detailed FAQ for every role of the workspace (English and Urdu), the bounded keyboard zoom and a named human's review with newly created data (get_guide('workspace-review-checklist')), signed on the portal. Missing any one, the workspace is NOT done: report it as pending, never as complete.

acceptance_rules: Clear the PharmacyClearance discharge stage once the patient's unused medicines are returned.

Read discharge-status to confirm the patient identity and blocked_on PharmacyClearance before clearing. After a lost answer re-read the stage's status, cleared_by_name and cleared_at there; never retry automatically.

A high-alert line (high_alert_category): a second person (pharmacist, or the nurse or doctor collecting it) checks the order and the medicine and co-signs with checker_username/_password (HIGH_ALERT_CHECK_REQUIRED; DUAL_CONTROL_SAME_PERSON). Show lasa_with next to the medicine: 'looks like …'.
After dispensing print one label per medicine: GET /dispensations/{dispensation_id}/labels (label printer).
PRESCRIPTION_QUERY_OPEN: the line waits for the doctor's answer to a query (Order queries screen).
Never let the user pick a batch — FEFO is server-side.
OPD pharmacy is cash-and-carry; credit only via approved Zakat/charity (charity_approval_id).

Cash goes into the user's own open shift at the Pharmacy Counter only: before offering Cash, GET /finance/cash-shifts/mine?node=PharmacyCounter. Null: Cash unavailable until it is opened on My cash shift (Card still works). SHIFT_NOT_OPEN with details.open_shift: the user's drawer is open at another counter (details.open_shift.node), which pharmacy cash never goes into; say so, never borrow another person's shift.

Exists for the service dispensing (work): show it as GET /establishment views.screens says for screen_id dispense (full; open_work: without its new work, with the banner "No new ... from now on"; records: history and corrections only; setup: only from Facility settings; hidden: in no menu), after login and again on establishment.changed. Never decide it from the profile's category.
POST /prescriptions/{prescription_id}/dispense continues dispensing work started earlier: offer it while dispensing is Active or Retiring (GET /establishment).
test_plan.demo_accounts: demo_accounts() lists a login per role; sandbox_call runs each case on the DEV server

sections: Step by step (one per task, where to click)

requirements.title: Purpose and audience
requirements.instruction:
Explain what this screen accomplishes, when to use it, who uses it and how to open it. State the patient, visit,
shift or other context the user must verify. Name the expected result in staff language.

requirements.title: Step by step (one per task, where to click)
requirements.instruction:
For every supported task give prerequisites, permissions or approvals, exact navigation and control labels,
what to enter or select, validation, the ordered steps and how to recognize completion. Include demo screenshots,
printed output and the next task or handover. Link to the corresponding workspace FAQ answer.

requirements.title: Every control and its effects
requirements.instruction:
Maintain a control inventory covering buttons, fields, selectors, tabs, menus, filters, sorting, scanners, shortcuts,
dialogs and navigation. For each user-facing control explain its label and purpose, when it is available, required
input, immediate effect, whether it saves or only changes the view, any confirmation, and what cancellation does.
Describe resulting data/state changes, notifications, printed output and consequences for other staff where relevant.
Include controls without API calls. Group repeated controls only when their behaviour is genuinely identical.

requirements.title: States and feedback
requirements.instruction:
Explain loading, no results, pending approval, success, stale data, denied actions and unavailable services. Describe
automatic realtime updates and how staff recognize that displayed information has changed. Explain disabled controls
and how to meet their prerequisites. Document only states and effects the implemented UI and backend support.

requirements.title: Messages, mistakes and recovery
requirements.instruction:
Explain the messages staff can encounter, why an action is refused and the permitted next step. Cover corrections,
duplicate clicks, a lost reply, concurrent changes, leaving unsaved work, session expiry, lost connection and printer
or scanner problems where applicable. Say what may have been saved, what to check before retrying and whom to contact.
Never promise unsupported undo or automatic offline submission. Use staff wording, not API paths or JSON.

requirements.title: Language and visual examples
requirements.instruction:
Supply English and Urdu pages matching the app's labels and reading direction, with legible demo-data screenshots
for each task and no real patient information. Keep terminology consistent across UI, FAQs and screenshots. Record
translation review status; a draft must not be represented as approved clinical wording.

requirements.title: Related help and delivery
requirements.instruction:
Link to the role's workspace guide, related tasks and handovers. F1 and contextual Help must open this screen's page.
Verify offline access, search, deep links, print-friendly output and the server's permission filtering. Update the
page, control inventory and FAQ links in the same release as the UI; retain the review evidence required by Q6.

workflows.title: Facility settings: the PHC profile and the clinical services
Cash shifts, payables, receivables, owner dashboards & risk

decisions.question: Digits in the Urdu UI and printouts: Latin 0-9 or Extended Arabic-Indic ۰-۹.
decisions.meanwhile: Latin digits; identifiers, doses and money stay left to right.

decisions.question: How dates and times are shown on screen, and a 12- or 24-hour clock.
decisions.meanwhile: The server's print format (e.g. 27-Sep-2026) and the hospital time zone.

decisions.question: Money on screen: decimals shown, and digit grouping (1,234,567 or 12,34,567).
decisions.meanwhile: The amounts as the API sends them, with the currency setting.

decisions.question: Who writes and signs off the Urdu text of the UI, above all clinical and consent wording.
decisions.meanwhile: Urdu you add is a draft: mark it so (the interview bank's pattern: a draft until a native speaker reviews it).

decisions.question: One design system shared by every frontend team (who authors and approves it), or each team's own.
decisions.meanwhile: Each team designs within the backend's constraints: themes Light and DarkHighContrast, zoom 100-250 %, Noto Nastaliq Urdu, status shown as text and icon, never colour alone. Follow the vendor's design principles (frontend guide 18, get_design_principles).

decisions.question: How each realtime event is shown (interrupt, attention, inform, silent), alert sounds and which terminals play them. Only Code Red (interrupt), the licence and maintenance banners and the logout on session.revoked are prescribed (the event catalogue's `presentation`).
decisions.meanwhile: Code Red interrupts; every other event updates the screen and, at most, a dismissible notice. `priority` is the delivery urgency, not a presentation rule.

decisions.question: May the second checker of a high-alert medicine use a badge and PIN instead of a username and password?
decisions.meanwhile: Username and password, never stored by the app.

decisions.question: Which workspaces run on web, Android and iOS, which cannot read a MAC address, discover the server by UDP or print silently; or are cash and printing Windows-only.
decisions.meanwhile: The guides describe the Windows (Electron) terminal; tell your developer when a screen needs a capability your platform lacks.

decisions.question: Tall-man names for look-alike medicines (a field on the drug master).
decisions.meanwhile: The look-alike pairs the API already returns.

decisions.question: Noto Nastaliq Urdu everywhere, or the more compact Naskh in dense tables.
decisions.meanwhile: Noto Nastaliq Urdu, as the guides require.

decisions.question: Allergies: the patient record keeps free text, so it cannot tell "no known allergies" (asserted by a clinician) from "not recorded". Should it?
affects: every screen with a patient banner
decisions.meanwhile: Show the recorded text as recorded; an empty value is "not recorded", never "none".

decisions.question: May unsaved form input be kept on the terminal (which fields, encrypted, for how long)?
decisions.meanwhile: In memory only; never a second checker's password.

decisions.question: Which documents may print on an unregistered terminal's default printer (sensitive A4 documents).
decisions.meanwhile: As the printing guide says: the hint, then the default printer.

decisions.question: Who approves frontend performance targets, alert thresholds and escalation timers.

details_stamp.description: Who recorded the reason and diagnosis, and when (MSDS 147)

text.title: Text

AuthorStampOut.title: AuthorStampOut
AuthorStampOut.description:
The author stamp of a clinical entry (MSDS IMS 147), as the author's staff record stood when they signed it
(SQL hms_author_stamp / hms_employee_stamp, migration 0013 [STP]). Show it under the entry on screen and print
`text` under it on paper.

opening_float.title: Opening Float
opening_float.description: The cash the drawer started with, issued from the main vault: the drawer's first entry (OpeningFloat)

expected_cash.title: Expected Cash
expected_cash.description: What the drawer should hold now: the opening float plus every cash movement of the shift (by_type). Count all of it at the close. 0 once the verified cash drop has taken it to the vault (cash_drop.expected_cash keeps the amount)

declared_cash.title: Declared Cash
declared_cash.description: What the cashier counted in the whole drawer at the close, the float included (null while open)

declared_variance.title: Declared Variance
declared_variance.description: declared_cash minus what the drawer held at the close, its float included (null until the shift is closed)

CashShiftSummaryOut.title: CashShiftSummaryOut
CashShiftSummaryOut.description: A shift with the expected cash by transaction type, non-cash collections and its cash drop.

blocked_on.title: Blocked On

blocked_on.title: Blocked On
blocked_on.description: The first pending stage (the one to clear next)

DischargeStatusViewOut.title: DischargeStatusViewOut
DischargeStatusViewOut.description: Identity and clearance progress for the staff clearing a stage, without the full clinical admission.

checked_by.title: Checked By

payment.description: Null when billed to the admission (IPD) or nothing to collect

checker_username.title: Checker Username

reverses_item_id.title: Reverses Item Id

server_time.title: Server Time

order_mode.title: Order Mode

prescriber_stamp.description: The prescriber when prescribing (MSDS 147; printed on the slip)

handovers.title: Handovers

drug_id.title: Drug Id

self_administration.title: Self Administration
self_administration.description: The doctor allowed the patient to take it themselves (MSDS 70)

lasa_with.title: Lasa With

drug_name.title: Drug Name
drug_name.description: The queried line's medicine (null for the whole prescription)

PrescriptionQueryOut.title: PrescriptionQueryOut
PrescriptionQueryOut.description: The pharmacist's query on an order (MSDS 51 iv), with the order it is about.

unknowns.question: Digits in the Urdu UI and printouts: Latin 0-9 or Extended Arabic-Indic ۰-۹.
unknowns.meanwhile: Latin digits; identifiers, doses and money stay left to right.

unknowns.question: How dates and times are shown on screen, and a 12- or 24-hour clock.
unknowns.meanwhile: The server's print format (e.g. 27-Sep-2026) and the hospital time zone.

unknowns.question: Money on screen: decimals shown, and digit grouping (1,234,567 or 12,34,567).
unknowns.meanwhile: The amounts as the API sends them, with the currency setting.

unknowns.question: Who writes and signs off the Urdu text of the UI, above all clinical and consent wording.
unknowns.meanwhile: Urdu you add is a draft: mark it so (the interview bank's pattern: a draft until a native speaker reviews it).

unknowns.question: One design system shared by every frontend team (who authors and approves it), or each team's own.
unknowns.meanwhile: Each team designs within the backend's constraints: themes Light and DarkHighContrast, zoom 100-250 %, Noto Nastaliq Urdu, status shown as text and icon, never colour alone. Follow the vendor's design principles (frontend guide 18, get_design_principles).

unknowns.question: How each realtime event is shown (interrupt, attention, inform, silent), alert sounds and which terminals play them. Only Code Red (interrupt), the licence and maintenance banners and the logout on session.revoked are prescribed (the event catalogue's `presentation`).
unknowns.meanwhile: Code Red interrupts; every other event updates the screen and, at most, a dismissible notice. `priority` is the delivery urgency, not a presentation rule.

unknowns.question: May the second checker of a high-alert medicine use a badge and PIN instead of a username and password?
unknowns.meanwhile: Username and password, never stored by the app.

unknowns.question: Which workspaces run on web, Android and iOS, which cannot read a MAC address, discover the server by UDP or print silently; or are cash and printing Windows-only.
unknowns.meanwhile: The guides describe the Windows (Electron) terminal; tell your developer when a screen needs a capability your platform lacks.

unknowns.question: Tall-man names for look-alike medicines (a field on the drug master).
unknowns.meanwhile: The look-alike pairs the API already returns.

unknowns.question: Noto Nastaliq Urdu everywhere, or the more compact Naskh in dense tables.
unknowns.meanwhile: Noto Nastaliq Urdu, as the guides require.

unknowns.question: May unsaved form input be kept on the terminal (which fields, encrypted, for how long)?
